content:
Crop: Paddy (Rice) (Kharif)
Soil & Climate: Clayey loam to silty clay soils with good water retention capacity. Optimum soil pH 5.5 to 7.0. Temperature range 22-32°C.
Sowing & Spacing: Direct seeded: 40-50 kg/ha. Transplanted: 20-25 kg/ha. Spacing: 20 cm x 15 cm. Optimal nursery sowing is May-June, transplanting at 21-25 days old seedlings.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices 2023-24

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices
metadata.reviewer_note: Standard ICAR-IIRR package of practices; nitrogen split doses and herbicide timings verified.

content:
Crop: Paddy (Rice) Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
Recommended NPK: 120:60:40 kg/ha. Apply 50% N and full P & K as basal dose before final puddling. Remaining N in two equal splits at tillering and panicle initiation stages. Zinc sulfate @ 25 kg/ha in zinc deficient soils.
Water Management: Maintain shallow water depth of 2-5 cm from transplanting till dough stage. Drain water 10-12 days before harvest.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices 2023-24

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices
metadata.reviewer_note: Standard ICAR-IIRR package of practices; nitrogen split doses and herbicide timings verified.

content:
Crop: Paddy (Rice) Weed Control:
Pre-emergence application of Pretilachlor 50% EC @ 1000-1500 ml/ha at 3-5 days after transplanting in standing water.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when 80-85% grains in panicles turn golden yellow and grain moisture is around 20%.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices 2023-24

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices
metadata.reviewer_note: Standard ICAR-IIRR package of practices; nitrogen split doses and herbicide timings verified.

content:
Crop: Wheat (Rabi)
Soil & Climate: Well-drained fertile loamy to clay loam soils. Optimum pH 6.0 to 7.5. Cool winter climate with 15-20°C at vegetative growth and 25°C at maturity.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 100-125 kg/ha for timely sown; 125-150 kg/ha for late sown. Spacing: 20-22.5 cm row to row. Optimal sowing window: First fortnight of November.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin
metadata.reviewer_note: Critical irrigation stages (CRI 21 DAS) and weed management verified against IIWBR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Wheat Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
Recommended NPK: 120:60:40 kg/ha for irrigated conditions. 50% N + 100% P & K at sowing time. Remaining N in two equal splits after first and second irrigation.
Water Management: Critical irrigation stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) at 21 DAS (most critical), Tillering at 40-45 DAS, Late Jointing at 60-65 DAS, Flowering at 80-85 DAS, and Milking at 100-105 DAS.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin
metadata.reviewer_note: Critical irrigation stages (CRI 21 DAS) and weed management verified against IIWBR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Wheat Weed Control:
Post-emergence spray of Sulfosulfuron 75% WG @ 33 g/ha + surfactant at 30-35 DAS for mixed weed control.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when straw becomes dry and golden brown, grains become hard with moisture content below 12-14%.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Advisory Bulletin
metadata.reviewer_note: Critical irrigation stages (CRI 21 DAS) and weed management verified against IIWBR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Tomato (Kharif / Rabi / Summer)
Soil & Climate: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam rich in organic matter. Soil pH 6.0-7.0. Sensitive to frost; thrives in 21-28°C daytime temperature.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 400-500 g/ha for open-pollinated; 120-150 g/ha for hybrids. Spacing: 60 cm x 45 cm for determinate varieties; 75 cm x 60 cm for indeterminate varieties.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Drip irrigation and hybrid NPK ratios verified with ICAR-IIHR vegetable production manuals.

content:
Crop: Tomato Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
FYM @ 20-25 tonnes/ha. NPK: 150:100:100 kg/ha for hybrids. Apply 50% N and full P & K as basal. Remaining N top-dressed in 2-3 equal splits at 30, 45, and 60 days after transplanting.
Water Management: Drip irrigation recommended. Water at 3-5 days interval during summer and 7-10 days interval during winter. Avoid water stagnation to prevent bacterial wilt.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Drip irrigation and hybrid NPK ratios verified with ICAR-IIHR vegetable production manuals.

content:
Crop: Tomato Weed Control:
Mulching with 25-30 micron silver-black UV polyethylene mulch suppresses weeds and conserves moisture.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest at 'breaker stage' for long-distance transport, and at pink to red ripe stage for local retail markets.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Drip irrigation and hybrid NPK ratios verified with ICAR-IIHR vegetable production manuals.

content:
Crop: Cotton (Kharif)
Soil & Climate: Deep black cotton soils (vertisols) or alluvial soils with high water retention. Soil pH 6.5-8.0. Requires long frost-free periods and warm sunny days (25-35°C).
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 2-2.5 kg/ha for Bt hybrids. Spacing: 90 cm x 60 cm or 120 cm x 45 cm depending on soil fertility and canopy.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Technology Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Integrated Pest Management Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Bt cotton canopy management and foliar DAP spray verified with CICR advisory.

content:
Crop: Cotton Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
NPK: 120:60:60 kg/ha. Split nitrogen into 3 equal doses: basal, squaring stage, and peak flowering stage. Foliar spray of 2% DAP or 1% KNO3 during boll development increases boll retention.
Water Management: Moisture stress at flowering and boll formation causes square and boll shedding. Avoid over-irrigation during early vegetative phase.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Technology Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Integrated Pest Management Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Bt cotton canopy management and foliar DAP spray verified with CICR advisory.

content:
Crop: Cotton Weed Control:
Pre-emergence Pendimethalin 38.7% CS @ 1.5-2.0 L/ha followed by inter-cultivation at 30 and 60 DAS.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Pick clean, fully opened bolls during dry morning hours. Keep picked cotton free of trash, dry leaves, and moisture.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Technology Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Integrated Pest Management Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Bt cotton canopy management and foliar DAP spray verified with CICR advisory.

content:
Crop: Maize (Corn) (Kharif / Rabi)
Soil & Climate: Deep, fertile, well-drained loamy to sandy loam soils with pH 6.5-7.5. Maize cannot tolerate waterlogging. Warm temperature 21-30°C.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 20 kg/ha for grain hybrids. Spacing: 60 cm x 20 cm at 3-5 cm depth.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Extension Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Crop Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: NPK 120:60:40 and FAW management verified with ICAR-IIMR bulletins.

content:
Crop: Maize (Corn) Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
NPK: 120:60:40 kg/ha. Apply 1/3 N and full P & K as basal dose. Apply 1/3 N at knee-high stage and remaining 1/3 N at tasseling stage.
Water Management: Critical stages for irrigation: Knee-high stage, Tasseling stage, and Silking/Grain-filling stage. Ensure effective field drainage during heavy rains.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Extension Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Crop Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: NPK 120:60:40 and FAW management verified with ICAR-IIMR bulletins.

content:
Crop: Maize (Corn) Weed Control:
Atrazine 50% WP @ 1.0-1.5 kg/ha applied as pre-emergence within 2-3 days of sowing.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when outer cob husk turns brown, grain moisture drops to 20-22%, and a black layer forms at the grain base.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Extension Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Crop Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: NPK 120:60:40 and FAW management verified with ICAR-IIMR bulletins.

content:
Crop: Sugarcane (Autumn / Spring / Eksali)
Soil & Climate: Deep well-drained loamy soils rich in organic matter with pH 6.5-7.5. Hot and humid climate with 28-35°C during tillering and sunny dry weather during maturity.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 35,000-40,000 three-budded setts/ha. Spacing: 90 cm to 120 cm row-to-row or paired row planting (60:120 cm) for drip.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Trichoderma settling dip and trash mulching verified against IISR cultivation practices.

content:
Crop: Sugarcane Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
Recommended NPK: 250:100:125 kg/ha. Apply full P and 1/3 K at planting. Split N into 3 doses: 25% at 30 DAP, 50% at 60 DAP, and 25% at 90 DAP along with earthing up. Ferrous sulfate @ 25 kg/ha in calcic soils.
Water Management: Critical stages: Formative phase (60-120 days) and Grand growth phase. Trash mulching @ 3.5 tonnes/ha retains soil moisture and saves 20-30% irrigation.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Trichoderma settling dip and trash mulching verified against IISR cultivation practices.

content:
Crop: Sugarcane Weed Control:
Atrazine 50% WP @ 2.0 kg/ha or Metribuzin 70% WP @ 1.0 kg/ha as pre-emergence within 3 days of sett planting.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when bottom leaves turn dry, stalk produces metallic sound on tapping, and hand refractometer brix reading reaches 18-20%.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR) Lucknow Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Trichoderma settling dip and trash mulching verified against IISR cultivation practices.

content:
Crop: Soybean (Kharif)
Soil & Climate: Well-drained fertile clay loams or black vertisols with pH 6.0-7.5. Warm climate with 25-30°C temperature; sensitive to waterlogging.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 65-75 kg/ha for bold seeds, 50-60 kg/ha for medium seeds. Spacing: 45 cm x 5-7 cm. Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium japonicum + PSB @ 5 g/kg seed.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Guidelines

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Rhizobium seed inoculation and pre-emergence pendimethalin verified.

content:
Crop: Soybean Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
NPK: 20:60:40 kg/ha basal dose along with 20 kg/ha Sulphur (Gypsum @ 150 kg/ha). Since soybean is a legume, nitrogen fixation fulfills subsequent N demand.
Water Management: Two critical irrigation stages if rainfall fails: Flowering stage (35-45 DAS) and Pod-filling stage (60-70 DAS). Waterlogging during seedling stage causes collar rot.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Guidelines

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Rhizobium seed inoculation and pre-emergence pendimethalin verified.

content:
Crop: Soybean Weed Control:
Pre-emergence Diclosulam 84% WDG @ 26-30 g/ha or post-emergence Imazethapyr 10% SL @ 1.0 L/ha at 15-20 DAS when weeds are in 2-3 leaf stage.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when 85-90% of pods turn golden yellow to brown and leaves start dropping. Moisture content of grain should be 13-15% to avoid shattering.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Guidelines

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR) Indore Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Rhizobium seed inoculation and pre-emergence pendimethalin verified.

content:
Crop: Groundnut (Peanut) (Kharif / Rabi / Summer)
Soil & Climate: Sandy loam, loamy sand, or well-drained light alluvial soil with pH 6.0-7.5. Calcium-rich soil essential for pod filling. Warm weather 24-30°C.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 100-110 kg/ha kernels for bunch types; 95-100 kg/ha for spreading types. Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm. Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Production Package

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Gypsum application at pegging and Trichoderma seed dressing verified.

content:
Crop: Groundnut (Peanut) Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
NPK: 25:50:50 kg/ha as basal. Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha in two splits: 200 kg as basal and 200 kg at pegging/flowering stage (40-45 DAS) to supply calcium and sulphur for pod formation.
Water Management: Critical stages: Flowering, Peg penetration, and Pod development. Avoid moisture stress between 40-70 days.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Production Package

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Gypsum application at pegging and Trichoderma seed dressing verified.

content:
Crop: Groundnut (Peanut) Weed Control:
Pendimethalin 30% EC @ 1.0 L a.i./ha as pre-emergence followed by one hand weeding at 20-25 DAS before peg initiation.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Pull sample plants; harvest when inner shell develops dark brown reticulation and kernels show typical seed coat color. Dry pods in sun to 8% moisture for storage.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Production Package

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Gypsum application at pegging and Trichoderma seed dressing verified.

content:
Crop: Mustard (Rapeseed) (Rabi)
Soil & Climate: Sandy loam to clay loam soils with good internal drainage. Soil pH 6.0-7.5. Cool winter climate (15-25°C); requires clear bright sunshine.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 3.5-4.0 kg/ha. Spacing: 30-45 cm x 10-15 cm. Optimal sowing time: 1st to 20th October.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur Package of Practices

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur
metadata.reviewer_note: Sulfur requirement (40 kg/ha) and aphid economic threshold verified with DRMR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Mustard (Rapeseed) Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
Recommended NPK: 80:40:40 kg/ha + 30 kg/ha Sulphur (via single superphosphate or bentonite sulphur). 50% N and full P, K, and S at sowing; remaining N after first irrigation.
Water Management: Irrigate at 25-30 DAS (Rosette / Pre-flowering stage) and 55-60 DAS (Siliqua formation stage). Moisture stress during flowering drastically cuts oil yield.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur Package of Practices

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur
metadata.reviewer_note: Sulfur requirement (40 kg/ha) and aphid economic threshold verified with DRMR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Mustard (Rapeseed) Weed Control:
Pre-plant incorporation or pre-emergence spray of Pendimethalin 30% EC @ 1.0 kg a.i./ha within 2 days of sowing.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest early in the morning when 75% of siliquae (pods) turn golden yellow to avoid shattering losses.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur Package of Practices

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) Bharatpur
metadata.reviewer_note: Sulfur requirement (40 kg/ha) and aphid economic threshold verified with DRMR guidelines.

content:
Crop: Potato (Rabi / Autumn)
Soil & Climate: Loose, friable sandy loam rich in organic matter. Soil pH 5.2-6.5. Cool sunny days (20-24°C) for vegetative growth and 16-20°C night temperature for tuberization.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed tuber rate: 2.5-3.0 tonnes/ha (tubers 35-45 mm diameter, 40-50 g weight). Spacing: 60 cm x 20 cm on ridges.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Seed tuber treatment with boric acid 3% and early earthing-up verified.

content:
Crop: Potato Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
FYM @ 25-30 tonnes/ha. NPK: 150:100:120 kg/ha. 50% N and full P & K as basal dose in furrows. Remaining 50% N applied at earthing up (30 DAS).
Water Management: First light irrigation immediately after planting. Subsequent irrigations every 7-10 days depending on soil texture. Stop irrigation 10-12 days before dehaulming.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Seed tuber treatment with boric acid 3% and early earthing-up verified.

content:
Crop: Potato Weed Control:
Metribuzin 70% WP @ 0.5-0.75 kg/ha applied within 3-5 days after planting or pre-emergence.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Dehaulming (cutting green foliage) 10-15 days before digging allows tuber skins to cure and harden, preventing bruising and post-harvest rot.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory Bulletin

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Seed tuber treatment with boric acid 3% and early earthing-up verified.

content:
Crop: Onion (Kharif / Late Kharif / Rabi)
Soil & Climate: Well-drained deep friable loamy soil with pH 6.0-7.0. Requires mild climate (13-24°C vegetative, 25-30°C for bulb development). Long daylight promotes bulb size.
Sowing & Spacing: Nursery seed rate: 8-10 kg/ha. Transplant 6-7 week old seedlings at 15 cm x 10 cm on raised beds.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Nursery management, thrips control, and curing guidelines verified with DOGR.

content:
Crop: Onion Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
FYM @ 20 tonnes/ha. NPK: 100:50:80 kg/ha + 30 kg/ha Sulphur. Apply 50% N and full P, K, S as basal. Remaining N top-dressed in 2 equal splits at 30 and 45 days after transplanting.
Water Management: Shallow frequent irrigations at 5-7 days interval. Drip irrigation saves 35-40% water and boosts bulb grading. Stop irrigation 15 days before harvest to avoid neck rot.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Nursery management, thrips control, and curing guidelines verified with DOGR.

content:
Crop: Onion Weed Control:
Oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC @ 1.5-2.0 ml/L or Pendimethalin 30% EC @ 3 ml/L pre-transplant or within 3 days of transplanting.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest when 50% of the plants show 'neck fall' (tops collapse). Field cure in rows for 3-5 days under shade followed by 10-15 days shed drying before storage.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Pune Advisory
metadata.reviewer_note: Nursery management, thrips control, and curing guidelines verified with DOGR.

content:
Crop: Chilli (Kharif / Rabi / Summer)
Soil & Climate: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam with pH 6.5-7.5. Warm humid climate (20-30°C); sensitive to heavy frost and water stagnation.
Sowing & Spacing: Seed rate: 1.0 kg/ha for varieties, 200-250 g/ha for hybrids. Spacing: 60 cm x 45 cm for rainfed, 75 cm x 45 cm for irrigated hybrids.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Chilli Production Technology

metadata.source_title: ICAR-IIHR Chilli Crop Production and Protection Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Murda complex (thrips/mites) and upward curling management verified.

content:
Crop: Chilli Fertilizer & Nutrient Management:
FYM @ 15-20 tonnes/ha. NPK: 120:60:60 kg/ha for irrigated crops. Apply 50% N and full P & K as basal; split remaining N into 3 doses at 30, 60, and 90 DAT.
Water Management: Irrigate at 6-8 days interval in winter, 4-5 days interval in summer. Water stagnation causes severe Phytophthora root rot.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Chilli Production Technology

metadata.source_title: ICAR-IIHR Chilli Crop Production and Protection Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: Murda complex (thrips/mites) and upward curling management verified.

content:
Crop: Chilli Weed Control:
Pre-emergence Pendimethalin 30% EC @ 2.5 L/ha followed by one hand weeding at 30 DAT.
Harvesting & Maturity:
Harvest green chillies when fully grown and pungent. For dry red chillies, harvest when fruits turn deep red ripe.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Chilli Production Technology

metadata.reviewer_note: Murda complex (thrips/mites) and upward curling management verified.

content:
Crop: Paddy (Rice) | Problem: How to control Yellow Stem Borer causing dead hearts and white ears in rice?
Hindi Query: धान में तना छेदक (डेड हार्ट और सफेद बालियां) की रोकथाम कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಭತ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಂಡ ಕೊರೆಯುವ ಹುಳುವಿನ ಹಾನಿಯನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸುವುದು?
Symptoms: Dead heart in vegetative stage (drying of central shoot); white head or empty chaffy panicle in reproductive stage.
Recommended Management & Control: Install pheromone traps @ 8-10 traps/ha for monitoring. Biological: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum @ 100,000/ha at 30, 37, and 44 DAT. Chemical control: Broadcast Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 10 kg/ha or spray Cartap Hydrochloride 50% SP @ 1000 g/ha or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 50 ml/ha in 500 liters of water per hectare.
Preventive Measures: Avoid excessive nitrogen application. Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to eliminate egg masses.
source: Kisan Call Centre (KCC) Advisory / ICAR-IIRR Pest Management Guide

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Package of Practices
metadata.reviewer_note: Standard ICAR-IIRR package of practices; nitrogen split doses and herbicide timings verified.

content:
Crop: Maize (Corn) | Problem: How to manage Fall Armyworm (FAW) Spodoptera frugiperda in maize whorls?
Hindi Query: मक्का में फॉल आर्मीवॉर्म (सैनिक कीट) का नियंत्रण कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಮೆಕ್ಕೆಜೋಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಲದ್ದಿ ಹುಳು (ಫಾಲ್ ಆರ್ಮಿವರ್ಮ್) ಹಾನಿ ತಡೆಗಟ್ಟುವುದು ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Pin-hole damage on leaves, ragged elongated holes on whorl leaves, large piles of sawdust-like fecal matter inside central whorl.
Recommended Management & Control: Early stage (5-30 days): Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kurstaki formulation @ 2 g/L or Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 5 ml/L into the whorl. Mid/Late stage: Spray Emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5 ml/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 ml/L directing the spray directly into the whorl cone.
Preventive Measures: Deep summer plowing to expose pupae to birds. Intercropping maize with pulses (cowpea/pigeon pea). Handpicking egg masses in smallholder fields.
source: Kisan Call Centre (KCC) Integrated Pest Management Advisory

metadata.source_title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Crop Production Guide
metadata.reviewer_note: NPK 120:60:40 and FAW management verified with ICAR-IIMR bulletins.

content:
Crop: Tomato | Problem: Tomato leaves are curling upwards with yellow margins and stunted growth. What is the remedy?
Hindi Query: टमाटर के पत्ते ऊपर की ओर मुड़ रहे हैं और पौधे बौने रह गए हैं, क्या उपाय करें?
Kannada Query: ಟೊಮೆಟೊ ಎಲೆಗಳು ಮುದುರಿಕೊಂಡು ಹಳದಿಯಾಗುತ್ತಿವೆ, ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಪರಿಹಾರವೇನು?
Symptoms: Severe curling, puckering, reduction of leaf lamina, yellowing of vein margins, bushy and stunted appearance caused by Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Recommended Management & Control: Control the whitefly vector immediately: Install yellow sticky traps @ 25-30/ha. Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L. Use Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2 ml/L as an organic deterrent.
Preventive Measures: Grow barrier crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet around the tomato plot. Use nursery nylon net (40-mesh) to raise virus-free seedlings. Uproot and burn severely infected plants.
source: KCC Query Database / ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Pathology Department

content:
Crop: Wheat | Problem: How to identify and control Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust) in wheat?
Hindi Query: गेहूं में पीला रतुआ (येलो रस्ट) की पहचान और नियंत्रण कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಗೋಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಳದಿ ರಸ್ಟ್ ರೋಗ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಮಾಡುವುದು ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Bright yellow powder pustules arranged in parallel stripes along leaf veins. Powder stains fingers when touched.
Recommended Management & Control: At first appearance of yellow pustules, immediately spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1 ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L in 500 liters of water per hectare. Repeat spray after 15 days if cloudy weather persists.
Preventive Measures: Sow rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g., HD 3086, DBW 187, DBW 222, PBW 725). Avoid delayed sowing after November 25.
source: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal Rust Advisory / Kisan Call Centre Bulletin

content:
Crop: Cotton | Problem: What are the chemical and bio-control measures for Pink Bollworm in cotton?
Hindi Query: कपास में गुलाबी सुंडी (पिंक बॉलवर्म) का रोकथाम कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಹತ್ತಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗುಲಾಬಿ ಕಾಯಿಕೊರೆಯುವ ಹುಳುವಿನ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆ ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Rosetted flowers that fail to open properly; bore holes sealed with frass; damaged seeds and stained lint inside green bolls.
Recommended Management & Control: Pheromone traps @ 12 traps/ha for mass trapping. Spray Profenofos 50% EC @ 2 ml/L or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2.5 ml/L or Thiodicarb 75% WP @ 2 g/L during peak emergence. For organic control, spray Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) @ 50 g/L.
Preventive Measures: Maintain a 'closed season' by terminating crop by December-January to prevent pest carryover. Avoid rationing.
source: Kisan Call Centre Advisory / CICR Nagpur Integrated Pest Management Protocol

content:
Crop: Paddy (Rice) | Problem: How to control Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) showing spindle-shaped spots with grey centres on leaves and rotten neck?
Hindi Query: धान में झुलसा रोग (राइस ब्लास्ट) की रोकथाम कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಭತ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಕುತ್ತಿಗೆ ರೋಗ (ಬ್ಲಾಸ್ಟ್ ರೋಗ) ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸುವುದು ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Spindle-shaped or eye-shaped lesions with ash-grey centers and dark brown margins on leaves; blackening and rotting of neck node causing falling of panicles.
Recommended Management & Control: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L (or 300-400 g/ha) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L or Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2.0 ml/L at first symptom. Spray at boot leaf and repeat at 10% flowering if weather is cloudy.
Preventive Measures: Avoid excessive doses of nitrogenous fertilizers; split nitrogen into 3-4 applications. Seed treatment with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed.
source: Kisan Call Centre (KCC) Query Logs / ICAR-IIRR Rice Pathology

content:
Crop: Tomato | Problem: How to treat Early Blight and Late Blight in tomato causing concentric rings and black rotting on leaves and fruits?
Hindi Query: टमाटर में अगेती और पछेती झुलसा (ब्लाइट) का इलाज कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಟೊಮೆಟೊ ಬೆಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಗಮಾರಿ (ಬ್ಲೈಟ್) ರೋಗ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Early Blight: Target-board concentric brown rings on older leaves. Late Blight: Water-soaked irregular dark brown lesions with white downy fungal growth on lower surface during humid weather.
Recommended Management & Control: Preventive: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L. Curative (at onset): Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L.
Preventive Measures: Ensure proper row spacing (60x45 cm) and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. Remove lower infected leaves and destroy.
source: KCC Technical Advisory / ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Pathology Division

content:
Crop: Groundnut (Peanut) | Problem: What is the control for Tikka disease (Cercospora leaf spot) in groundnut showing dark circular spots with yellow halo?
Hindi Query: मूंगफली में टिक्का रोग (पत्ती धब्बा) का नियंत्रण कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಕಡಲೆಕಾಯಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಟಿಕ್ಕಾ ಎಲೆಚುಕ್ಕೆ ರೋಗದ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Early leaf spot: Circular reddish-brown to dark spots surrounded by prominent yellow halo. Late leaf spot: Smaller, darker black spots without prominent yellow halo, causing premature defoliation.
Recommended Management & Control: Spray Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2 ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L or Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Saaf) @ 2 g/L in 500 liters water/ha. Repeat after 15 days.
Preventive Measures: Crop rotation with non-host crops (cereals). Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg or Thiram @ 3 g/kg.
source: Kisan Call Centre Advisory / ICAR-DGR Junagadh

content:
Crop: Chilli | Problem: Chilli leaf margins are curling upwards and boat-shaped with stunted flowering. How to control thrips and mites?
Hindi Query: मिर्च में पत्ता मरोड़, थ्रिप्स (चंपा) और माइट्स की रोकथाम कैसे करें?
Kannada Query: ಮೆಣಸಿನಕಾಯಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನುಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಹೇನು (ಥ್ರಿಪ್ಸ್) ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಹೇಗೆ?
Symptoms: Upward curling of leaves, crinkling, brittle texture caused by Thrips (Scirtothrips dorsalis); downward curling into inverted boat shape caused by yellow mites (Polyphagotarsonemus latus).
Recommended Management & Control: For Thrips (upward curl): Spray Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5-2.0 ml/L or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.9 ml/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.3 g/L. For Mites (downward curl): Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Fenpyroximate 5% EC @ 1.5 ml/L. Use Blue sticky traps @ 25/ha for thrips monitoring.
Preventive Measures: Intercrop with 2 rows of maize or sunflower as barrier crops. Spray Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/L at early vegetative stage.
source: ICAR-IISR Chilli Protection Guide / Kisan Call Centre Expert Panel

metadata.reviewer_note: Murda complex (thrips/mites) and upward curling management verified.

content:
Crop: Paddy / Wheat / Maize | Problem: Leaves are turning yellow/whitish with rusty brown spots and stunted growth. How to correct Zinc deficiency?
Hindi Query: फसलों में जिंक (जस्ता) की कमी और खैरा रोग के लक्षण और उपाय क्या हैं?
Kannada Query: ಬೆಳೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸತುವಿನ (ಜಿಂಕ್) ಕೊರತೆ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಹಾರವೇನು?
Symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young leaves, bronze or rusty brown pigmentation, reduced tillering, delayed flowering ('Khaira' disease in rice).
Recommended Management & Control: Foliar spray: Dissolve Zinc sulfate heptahydrate (21% Zn) @ 5 g + unslaked lime (chuna) @ 2.5 g (or urea @ 10 g) in 1 liter of water. Spray twice at 10-12 days interval on standing crop. For soil correction: Apply Zinc sulfate @ 25 kg/ha before sowing.
Preventive Measures: Conduct Soil Health Card test before sowing. Avoid combining high doses of phosphatic fertilizer (DAP) with zinc directly at the same time.
source: Kisan Call Centre Advisory / ICAR-Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS) Bhopal

content:
Scheme Name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
Summary: Income support scheme providing Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal four-monthly installments of Rs. 2,000 each directly transferred to the bank accounts of eligible landholder farmer families.
Eligibility Target Group: All landholding farmer families with cultivable landholding in their names.
Exclusions: Institutional landholders; Farmer families holding constitutional posts (former or present); Former and present Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, Mayors, Chairpersons of District Panchayats; Serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Govt Ministries/Offices/PSUs/Autonomous bodies (excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees); All superannuated/retired pensioners with monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more; All persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year; Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card (mandatory), Citizenship proof, Landholding papers (RoR / Khatauni / Pahani), Bank Account details linked with Aadhaar
Benefits: Rs. 6,000 per annum paid in 3 installments of Rs. 2,000 every 4 months (April-July, August-November, December-March) via DBT.
Application Process: Farmers can register online at the PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) using 'Farmer Corner', or through Common Service Centres (CSCs) or State Nodal Officers.
source: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) (Official Portal: https://pmkisan.gov.in)

content:
Scheme Name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
Summary: Comprehensive crop insurance scheme providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest.
Eligibility Target Group: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas including sharecroppers and tenant farmers. Voluntary for all farmers.
Exclusions: Crops not notified in the area by state government; Losses due to war, nuclear risks, malicious damage, theft, or domestic animals
Documents Required: Aadhaar Card, Land Record (Pahani / RTC / Land Possession Certificate), Sowing certificate issued by Patwari / Village Agriculture Worker / Revenue officer, Bank Passbook copy linked to Aadhaar
Benefits: Maximum premium payable by farmers is only 2% for all Kharif food & oilseeds crops, 1.5% for all Rabi food & oilseeds crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops. The remaining premium is shared 50:50 by Central and State Governments.
Application Process: Enrollment through National Crop Insurance Portal (pmfby.gov.in), authorized banks, or CSCs before cutoff date for Kharif (typically July 31) and Rabi (typically December 31).
source: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) (Official Portal: https://pmfby.gov.in)

Scheme Name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
Summary: Timely and hassle-free institutional short-term credit facility for farmers to meet cultivation expenses, post-harvest expenses, marketing loans, and working capital for maintenance of farm assets and allied activities (dairy, fisheries, poultry).
Eligibility Target Group: Individual/joint farmers, owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers.
Exclusions: Defaulters with existing unregularized institutional agricultural loans
Documents Required: Filled application form, ID Proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID / Driving License), Address Proof, Land ownership record / tenancy agreement, Passport size photographs
Benefits: Credit limit up to Rs. 3 Lakh at an effective interest rate of 4% per annum (standard interest rate 9%, with 2% interest subvention by GoI and 3% prompt repayment incentive). Collateral-free loan up to Rs. 1.6 Lakh (extendable to Rs. 2 Lakh for tie-up arrangements).
Application Process: Apply at any commercial bank, Regional Rural Bank (RRB), or Cooperative Bank branch, or online through state agri-credit portals.
source: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme (Official Portal: https://agricoop.nic.in)

Scheme Name: Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme
Summary: Periodic assessment of farm soil fertility status across 12 parameters (Macro: N, P, K; Secondary: S; Micro: Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo; Physical: pH, EC, OC) along with customized dosage recommendations for crops.
Eligibility Target Group: All farmers across all States and Union Territories in India.
Exclusions: None (universal entitlement for agricultural landholders)
Documents Required: Farmer identification details (Aadhaar), Survey number / plot identification of field sample
Benefits: Free soil test report issued every 3 years providing exact nutrient deficiency analysis and crop-specific fertilizer and organic manure recommendations to reduce input costs and preserve soil health.
Application Process: Soil samples collected by State Agriculture Department field officers and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). Farmers can download their card online using survey number at soilhealth.dac.gov.in.
source: Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme (Official Portal: https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in)
